results: 1. MRI of the head and forehead with contrast
MRI brain with gadolinium: cerebellar vermis hypoplasia with molar tooth sign; no abnormal enhancement
MRI cervical and thoracic spine: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Joubert syndrome

Alternative 1: Joubert syndrome-related disorder (JSRD) with orofacial digitation
Alternative 2: Meckel-Gruber syndrome (less likely given normal spinal imaging and no encephalocele)
Alternative 3: Isolated congenital bifid tongue with incidental molar tooth sign
order_raw:
Based on the visual evidence of a midline forehead pit (suggestive of a congenital dermoid sinus) and a bifid tongue, there is a risk of an intracranial connection to the sinus and an association with spinal dysraphism (tethered cord), which can occur even without visible skin markers on the back.
